source.title: Multiple Orderings of Events in Disease Progression.

confidence_rationale: Directly attacks the assumption INV-047 depends on -- that there is ONE staged sequence characterising the disease. Relaxing the single-sequence assumption with a generalised Mallows model shows substantially more cross-subject variation than the classic model estimates, and a Dirichlet process mixture detects three population subgroups following DIFFERENT event sequences. Confidence held at 0.58 because this is a methods paper on imaging events rather than cognitive stages, so it undermines the claim's form rather than its specific content.
failure_signatures: A Dirichlet process mixture recovers THREE distinct subgroups with different event sequences in sporadic AD. INV-047 asserts 'the specific staged cognitive decline profile' in the singular; if the population is a mixture of orderings, no single canonical profile is the thing to be explained.

The classic single-sequence event-based model UNDERSTATES cross-subject variation in ordering. Any prior staging result INV-047 leans on that was produced by the classic model therefore carries an unmodelled false confidence in its ordering.

Heterogeneity of this kind is an alternative explanation for apparent staging: a population mixture of differently-ordered subgroups can produce an averaged profile that looks staged without any subject following the average sequence.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Relaxing the event-based model's single-sequence assumption -- via a generalised Mallows model and a Dirichlet process mixture of such models -- reveals greater cross-subject variation in event ordering than previously estimated, and identifies three subgroups of the ADNI population following distinct sequences.
mapping.ree_translation: INV-047 treats the staged decline profile as a single explanandum with a determinate order to be matched against a phase-dependency ordering. This work indicates the explanandum may not be singular: sporadic AD appears to comprise subpopulations with different orderings. If so, a claim predicting ONE order is either underspecified or is a claim about a subgroup, and REE would need to say which.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The events modelled here are imaging/biomarker abnormalities in brain regions, NOT the cognitive stages INV-047 enumerates. Heterogeneity in regional atrophy ordering does not automatically imply heterogeneity in cognitive-stage ordering -- the cognitive phenotype could be more canalised than its neural substrate. This entry therefore weakens INV-047's single-sequence FORM by analogy and does not directly measure the cognitive orderings the claim is about. It is also a conference methods paper, with correspondingly lighter clinical validation.
mapping.source_context: Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) multi-modal biomarker data; cross-sectional; Gibbs sampling inference over generalised Mallows and Dirichlet process mixture models.

confidence_components.notes: Sound methodological work from the group that built the event-based model, published at IPMI (peer-reviewed conference, lighter than a journal). Scored as a moderate weakener: it challenges the singular-sequence framing INV-047 requires, but by analogy from imaging events rather than by direct measurement of cognitive stage orderings.
